poem.content:
In the stillness of a moonlit lake,
A deer's gentle form does softly shake,
A glimpse of life, a fleeting sight,
A moment's peace, before the dawn's first light.

The fork of a tree, a shaft of might,
Reaches for the stars, a guiding light,
A hungry soul, with heart aflame,
Yearns for a picnic, a love-filled game.

But soon, the gap between love and desire,
Grows wide, a chasm that cannot be fired,
A sword of doubt, a destructive blade,
 Threatens to destroy, the love we've made.

Yet, in the midst of this dark despair,
A glimpse of hope, a glimmering air,
A saddle worn, by a weary heart,
A call to inject, a new-found start.

In the parade of life, we march and sway,
With every step, a new path's made,
A fork in the road, a choice to take,
A decision that will soon make or break.

The dinner bell, a signal to dine,
A time to feast, on love's sweet wine,
A lake of memories, a reflection deep,
A glimpse of what we've yet to keep.

And when the night, with darkness falls,
The deer's soft form, will echo through the walls,
A reminder of love's gentle might,
A glimpse of hope, in the dark of night.
